title: Welcome, come in!
can_do: You can respond when you're welcomed into someone's home.

grammar.heading: Polite invitations
grammar.body: A good host says these the moment you arrive: `aaiye` is "please come" and `andar aaiye` is "come in". `baiThiye` is "please sit down". Learn them as whole chunks for now. You'll hear them all the time.

grammar.heading: "Will you have…?"
grammar.body: To offer something, name it and add `lenge?`: `chaae lenge?` is "will you have some tea?" Swap the first word to offer something else. `aur` also means "more", so `aur chaae lenge?` is "will you have more tea?" Your host may also say `lengii` to a woman; `lenge` is a safe polite form for anyone.

grammar.heading: Yes please, no thanks, enough
grammar.body: `jii, shukriyaa` accepts politely, and `jii nahiiN, shukriyaa` declines politely. When you've had enough, say `bas, shukriyaa`. Hosts usually offer again, so you may have to say it twice.

grammar.heading: Saying something nice
grammar.body: A small compliment goes a long way. `mazedaar` is "delicious" and `xuubsuurat` is "beautiful". Like `xush`, they never change.

exercises.prompt: Your aunty opens the door and says this. What does she mean?
Your host asks `chaae lenge?` You would like some tea. What do you say?

options.en: No, thank you. But you'd like some.
Goodbye. But you've only just sat down.

exercises.explanation: `jii, shukriyaa` is a polite yes. `jii` is doing the work of "yes" here.

exercises.prompt: You've finished your cup, and your host is offering more. You've had enough. What do you say?

options.en: Yes, of course! But you've had enough.
Will you have some tea? That's what your host says.

exercises.explanation: `bas` is what you say when you've had enough. `jii nahiiN, shukriyaa` is fine too; `bas` is just the natural word for stopping refills.
`chaae lenge?` is the polite offer. Learn it as a chunk for now.
`bas` means "enough" and politely stops the refills.
The word order is the same as `maiN bahut xush huuN`: `bahut` before the describing word, and the verb last.

sentence.en: Sit down, will you have some tea?

exercises.explanation: First the invitation, then the offer. `lenge` comes last, like any verb.
`huuN` only goes with `maiN`. The tea takes `hai`.
